input.add_to_description: Day 12 ~12:33 AM: statted as a Scout (16 HP, AC 13), called 'Prowler' in the tracker. Made his DEX save (13) against Wren's Faerie Fire and stayed unlit; ducked behind the water-butt in the shrine yard. Kit stands between him and the shrine door.

entries.text: notebook: updated Sparrow's Watcher

You ease the shutter open a finger's breadth and throw the spell across the yard. Violet light blooms around the hooded shape. Then it fades, as if the dark had shrugged. He made his save, a bare 13 against your DC 13, and he stays in shadow. Your slot is spent (two left), and you're concentrating on a spell that has no one in it.

You call out in your gruffest fishwife croak: "Ferry's closed till morning, friend! State your business or the hook comes down!" For a heartbeat there is only river noise. The hooded man goes absolutely still, a hand crossbow at his hip, thirty feet from your shutter. Whoever he is, he's no fool. He doesn't answer. He slides sideways behind the water-butt, one hand on the barrel, and you hear nothing more but the reeds.

Kit, who can't see him in this blackness, doesn't waste a bolt. She steps out of the byre door with her shield up and plants herself between the yard and the shrine's door. "Show yourself," she says, flat as a plank. "Or go home."

The fight has begun, though not a blow has landed. Round one is done, and it's your turn again. The prowler is hidden behind the water-butt, and Tamsin is a shadow near the ferry shed with her hook. Your Faerie Fire has about fifty seconds left, but it lights nothing. You have two slots, three Bardic Inspirations, and an open shutter.

What does Wren do?

sheet.name: Wren Ashgrove
sheet.opening: Wren Ashgrove, a half-elf bard of about nineteen with a quick grin and a sharper tongue, arrives at dusk in the river-market town of Marrowford, a few weeks after fleeing the caravan of her mentor Corvin Tallowmere. She was raised by him as a storyteller's apprentice, and she left in the night at a river crossing with his ledger of forged tales sold to nobles (its pages now hidden in the binding of her road-psalter), a few of his best forgeries, and a head start. She carries a brass lantern-shaped reliquary of the Lantern-Bearer, a gentle road-god of travelers and tale-tellers whom Corvin worshipped only as cover; it holds a curl of yellowed parchment in an unknown hand that may be a true blessing or another forgery. She does not know if Corvin has sent anyone after her. Her ideal: stories should be free, and truth is whatever people can be made to believe. Her bond: find the nobles Corvin cheated and decide whether to expose him or quietly fix what he did. Her flaw: she can't resist a secret, and she lies even when the truth would serve her better. She has 15 gp, a rapier, a dagger, leather armor, a lute, a diplomat's pack with blank paper and sealing wax, and was raised with no memory of her birth family. The hook: as she reaches the market square, she spots a caravan wagon with Corvin's painted shrine-lantern sigil parked at the edge of town, but no sign of Corvin. A frightened young page in a minor noble's livery is pressing a sealed letter into the hands of the wagon's driver, and the seal looks like one Wren has seen in the ledger. Something is happening that links her stolen ledger to a noble house, and it needs a quick-witted liar to either sort it out or be caught in it. Open on Wren in the square, with the choice of how to approach the wagon and the page, and a locked iron-bound strongbox on the wagon's tailboard that she itches to poke at.

traits: Playful, nosy, and can't resist poking at locked doors or odd-looking relics
A charming liar with a sharp tongue who will bluff through almost anything with a grin

Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. The creature can wait until after it rolls the d20 before deciding to use the Bardic Inspiration die, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle. You might also have ties to a specific temple dedicated to your chosen deity or pantheon, and you have a residence there. This could be the temple where you used to serve, if you remain on good terms with it, or a temple where you have found a new home. While near your temple, you can call upon the priests for assistance, provided the assistance you ask for is not hazardous and you remain in good standing with your temple.

input.add_to_description: Day 12 ~12:35 AM: resisted Wren's Faerie Fire (DEX save 16) and was not outlined; the spell lit the wall and water-butt around him instead. Stat block of a Scout (AC 13, 16 HP, shortsword and longbow). Challenged by Wren's fishwife voice, he froze, then stepped back toward the dark.

entries.text: notebook: updated Sparrow's Watcher

You ease the shutter open a finger's breadth, breathe the Lantern-Bearer's word, and throw your hand toward the hooded shape. Violet light blooms across the yard. It catches the water-butt, the byre wall and the wet shingle, and all of them glow like a stage set. One slot spent, two left. You are concentrating on the spell, and it will hold about a minute.

The man himself is another matter. He had to make a Dexterity save against your DC 13, and he rolled a 16. The light slides off him. He stands dim and half-lit in a ring of violet, hood up, shortsword and hand crossbow at his belt, a scout by the look of him and quick on his feet. He is not outlined, so Kit gets no advantage on him.

Then you call out in your gruff fishwife voice: "Ferry's closed till morning, friend! State your business or the hook comes down!"

He freezes. His head turns toward the shutter, then toward the byre, where he must guess a shield is waiting, and then toward the ferry shed, where Tamsin's hook has just shifted in the dark. He doesn't answer. His hand drifts to the crossbow and stops. He takes one slow step backward, out of the brightest part of the glow, and the dark behind him is open all the way to the dike.

He knows the house is awake, and he hasn't decided yet whether to run, shoot or talk. The light has about fifty seconds left. Kit's crossbow is up at the byre door, and Tamsin is a breath away from the hook coming down. What does Wren do?

line:
"Kit, get to the barn door and help the guards pull the prisoners out, and keep Corvin and Ansel together where you can see both. The fire is a lure, and the real move is behind the north hedge."

I run along the barn's shadow toward the north side, plant myself with my back to the wall so nothing can come up behind me, and cast Faerie Fire on the dark stretch of hedge where the burning rag came from, lighting up any hidden shapes. At the same time I shout, "Sparrow! You smile too much to be a good thief, so show yourself!"

input.add_to_description: Day 16 ~10:30 PM: fight at the farm barn. Wren cast Faerie Fire on the north hedge: Sparrow (save 10) and Raider 1 (10) are lit; Raider 2 (14) is not. Kit hauling prisoners clear of the burning barn; Pell's guards fighting the fire.

entries.text: notebook: updated Signal Lights on the River

"Kit, the door, and keep them together!" Kit is gone at a run, shield up, and you hear her voice and Pell's bellowing over the crackle of the thatch. You sprint along the barn's shadow, plant your back against the north wall, and throw out your hand at the black line of the hedge. "Sparrow! You smile too much to be a good thief, so show yourself!"

Faerie Fire blooms across the hedge. Sparrow's save is a 10 and one raider's is a 10, so both stand outlined in cold violet light, Sparrow crouched with a hand crossbow half raised and a broad man beside him with a scimitar. A third man had the luck to roll a 14, and he is only a darker shape in the dark, about ten feet to their left. The burning thatch throws orange light over all of it. Sparrow's smile is gone.

Kit rolled a 20 for initiative and is already at the barn door. Your spell took your action, and you hold it by concentration with two slots left. Sparrow is about thirty feet from you, and the raiders are close behind him. The fire is spreading along the roof, and the guards are shouting for buckets.

You still have your bonus action and your movement this turn. What does Wren do?
You have 17 of 17 hit points, two 1st-level slots, three Bardic Inspirations, a rapier, a dagger and the lamp-staff.

You smile too much to be a good thief, so show yourself!"

The light bursts out across the hedge. Sparrow's save is a 7, and a leaning figure in a brown coat lights up violet, crouched against the thorns with his hand crossbow half raised. Two broader shapes beside him, both with pikes, shrug it off (a 21 and a 20) and stay dark. The thatch roars overhead, the horses scream, and Pell's guards are all shouting at the front.

You acted first, at the top of round 1, and your action is spent on the spell. You still have your bonus action and some movement. You hold Faerie Fire by concentration, with two slots and three Bardic Inspirations left, at 17 of 17 hit points. Sparrow is lit and about forty feet off. The pikemen will come in right after you, and Kit won't reach the barn door until her turn. What does Wren do with the rest of her turn?

sheet.name: Wren Ashgrove
sheet.opening: Wren Ashgrove, a half-elf bard of about nineteen with a quick grin and a sharper tongue, arrives at dusk in the river-market town of Marrowford, a few weeks after fleeing the caravan of her mentor Corvin Tallowmere. She was raised by him as a storyteller's apprentice, and she left in the night at a river crossing with his ledger of forged tales sold to nobles (its pages now hidden in the binding of her road-psalter), a few of his best forgeries, and a head start. She carries a brass lantern-shaped reliquary of the Lantern-Bearer, a gentle road-god of travelers and tale-tellers whom Corvin worshipped only as cover; it holds a curl of yellowed parchment in an unknown hand that may be a true blessing or another forgery. She does not know if Corvin has sent anyone after her. Her ideal: stories should be free, and truth is whatever people can be made to believe. Her bond: find the nobles Corvin cheated and decide whether to expose him or quietly fix what he did. Her flaw: she can't resist a secret, and she lies even when the truth would serve her better. She has 15 gp, a rapier, a dagger, leather armor, a lute, a diplomat's pack with blank paper and sealing wax, and was raised with no memory of her birth family. The hook: as she reaches the market square, she spots a caravan wagon with Corvin's painted shrine-lantern sigil parked at the edge of town, but no sign of Corvin. A frightened young page in a minor noble's livery is pressing a sealed letter into the hands of the wagon's driver, and the seal looks like one Wren has seen in the ledger. Something is happening that links her stolen ledger to a noble house, and it needs a quick-witted liar to either sort it out or be caught in it. Open on Wren in the square, with the choice of how to approach the wagon and the page, and a locked iron-bound strongbox on the wagon's tailboard that she itches to poke at.

traits: Playful, nosy, and can't resist poking at locked doors or odd-looking relics
A charming liar with a sharp tongue who will bluff through almost anything with a grin

features: Darkvision: You have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.
Fey Ancestry: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic cannot put you to sleep.
Skill Versatility: You gain proficiency in two skills of your choice.

Bardic Inspiration (d6): You can inspire others through stirring words or music. To do so, you use a bonus action on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die, a d6. Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. The creature can wait until after it rolls the d20 before deciding to use the Bardic Inspiration die, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Once the Bardic Inspiration die is rolled, it is lost. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.  Your Bardic Inspiration die changes when you reach certain levels in this class. The die becomes a d8 at 5th level, a d10 at 10th level, and a d12 at 15th level. At level 2: Bardic Inspiration die d6.
Jack of All Trades: Starting at 2nd level, you can add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to any ability check you make that doesn't already include your proficiency bonus.

Song of Rest (d6): Beginning at 2nd level, you can use soothing music or oration to help revitalize your wounded allies during a short rest. If you or any friendly creatures who can hear your performance regain hit points at the end of the short rest by spending one or more Hit Dice, each of those creatures regains an extra 1d6 hit points.  The extra hit points increase when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d8 at 9th level, to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level. At level 2: extra 1d6 hit points.

Shelter of the Faithful (Acolyte): As an acolyte, you command the respect of those who share your faith, and you can perform the religious ceremonies of your deity. You and your adventuring companions can expect to receive free healing and care at a temple, shrine, or other established presence of your faith, though you must provide any material components needed for spells. Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle. You might also have ties to a specific temple dedicated to your chosen deity or pantheon, and you have a residence there. This could be the temple where you used to serve, if you remain on good terms with it, or a temple where you have found a new home. While near your temple, you can call upon the priests for assistance, provided the assistance you ask for is not hazardous and you remain in good standing with your temple.

spellcasting.notes: Spells known are fixed until a level-up.
